problems.source_says: The benchmark compares AI-only campaigns with human-AI campaigns produced during the assisted task. Given the retained construct='diversity' and ai_available_when_produced='yes', the codebook's explicit routing rule requires across_people, not none. The codebook supplies no exception to that rule for a context benchmark; keeping this comparison outside the core dataset does not support this question label.
problems.quote: Although all simulated campaigns (AI only) are high quality (scoring 8/10), they are consistently less creative than human-AI generated ones.
problems.locator: PDF p. 9, Fig. 2B caption; p. 10, Personalization as Pathway to Counteract AI-Based Homogenization; p. 21, Experimental Design; creativity-codebook.md section 1, especially line 17.

problems.source_says: The paper measures final-campaign length as word count, labels it Behavioral in Table S5, and distinguishes it from the adjacent LLM-assessed component and marketing-term counts. No scoring model or LLM judgment of campaign length is described. The codebook defines automated_score as a scoring model for creativity, so using it merely as the nearest computational category is unsupported even though the form discloses that approximation. The exact replacement code cannot be confirmed: the codebook's behavioral category is restricted to market or usage outcomes and supplies no plain-word-count category.
problems.locator: PDF p. 19, Participants, campaign-length statistics; PDF p. 61 (supplement p. 33), Table S5, Campaign Word Count row; creativity-codebook.md section 6, Measure, lines 98-99.

S1-O3 compares each campaign's GPT-4o-extracted themes with the pooled centroid of campaigns using text-embedding-3-large. This compares different participants' outputs and supports diversity/across_people and embedding_similarity, with one score per campaign rather than one observation per theme or pair.

summary: Criterion 3 holds because participants' submitted campaigns receive quality ratings and a computed cross-participant theme-similarity score. Two coding details are unsupported: S2-O1's question label conflicts with the codebook rule, and S1-O4's ordinary word count is classified as a scoring model.
